body.statement: Under the paper's standing assumption that the observational law \(P(V)\) is strictly positive, Chen--Darwiche Theorem 1 states that the state-specific causal effect \(P_x(y)\) is identifiable under the supplied context-specific independence constraints if Algorithm 1 returns a formula for estimating \(P_x(y)\).

source.verbatim_statement: We assume that the observational distribution Pr(V) is strictly positive, i.e., Pr(V)>0. Theorem 1. Let C be a set of CSI constraints. Then Pr_x(y) is identifiable wrt ⟨G,V,C⟩ if Algorithm 1 returns a formula for estimating Pr_x(y).
